title: Chest Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents to the emergency department with acute onset chest pain and severe respiratory distress. The patient appears diaphoretic, tachypneic, and in extremis. Symptoms began suddenly with rapid progression. Exam reveals unilateral absence of breath sounds, tracheal deviation, and hyperresonance on percussion. Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis made at the bedside — immediate intervention is critical and must not be delayed for imaging.
chief_complaint: Chest pain with severe respiratory distress

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: It is always important to see how the patient looks in general to assess how sick the patient is.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Evaluate chest/lungs in a patient with respiratory distress.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Cardiovascular evaluation provides key information in respiratory distress. Only focused exam needed in emergency.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine
stacks.finding: Symptoms could result from PE — evaluate extremities for signs of DVT.

stacks.label: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: Patient in respiratory distress — check pulse oximetry.

stacks.label: Electrocardiography, 12 lead
stacks.finding: Initial EKG to rule out myocardial infarction.

stacks.label: Cardiac troponin I, serum
stacks.finding: Troponins should be evaluated — patient has chest pain, MI must be ruled out.

stacks.label: Thoracentesis
stacks.finding: Good diagnostic step to confirm tension pneumothorax. However, chest tube must follow to prevent recurrence.

stacks.label: Tube thoracostomy / Needle thoracostomy
stacks.finding: Chest tube should be placed after needle thoracostomy and placed to suction.

stacks.label: Chest X-ray (post-procedure)
stacks.finding: X-ray verifies chest tube placement AFTER insertion. Do NOT diagnose by X-ray — tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis. Imaging before tube placement loses points.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Tachycardic; assess for muffled heart sounds and JVD.
physical_exam.respiratory: Unilateral absence of breath sounds. Tracheal deviation. Hyperresonance on affected side.

decoys.label: Chest X-ray (before intervention)
decoys.reason_wrong: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis. Imaging before decompression causes dangerous delay.

decoys.label: CT chest with contrast
decoys.reason_wrong: CT causes unacceptable delay in a life-threatening emergency.

decoys.label: Echocardiogram
decoys.reason_wrong: Too time-consuming. Immediate decompression is the priority.

decoys.label: D-dimer, serum
decoys.reason_wrong: While PE is on the differential, exam findings point to tension pneumothorax. Decompress first.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Clinical triad: tracheal deviation + absent breath sounds + hyperresonance. Hypotension and respiratory distress. Do NOT wait for imaging.
2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line. Converts tension to simple pneumothorax. Life-saving.
Follows needle decompression. Place to suction for definitive management.
Confirms tube position and lung re-expansion. Must be AFTER intervention, never before.

case_summary: Medical emergency. Clinical diagnosis of tension pneumothorax — needle decompression then chest tube, X-ray only after to verify placement. Admit for monitoring.
